title: MaxSource
description: MAXGEN 2.0 -- One MaxSource is one work, collection or repository that documents come from or are held by (a book, a periodical, a census collection, a microfilm publication, a family Bible, an archive, a library or a website), with what it covers and how to search it.

source_id.description: This source's own id: a random UUID created once by the writer and never reused.

name.description: The source's name in plain words, such as a made-up 'Tumblebrook parish registers, 1801-1900'.

source_type.description: What kind of source this is.

source_type_as_written.description: The kind of source in the writer's or the other program's own words, given when source_type is other.

redistribution_license.description: Whether this source entry may be shared (unclear means ask, never guess); a tier2-private entry never appears in any open dataset, share, export, public embedding or commit.

is_living_flag.description: Living A floor: true when this source entry names someone who may be alive, such as a privately held family Bible (unsure means true; credits never set it); true requires tier2-private.

source_url.description: The source's own address, when it has one; optional (a book or a family Bible has none) and never invented.

address.description: MAXGEN 2.1 (G-14): where an archive or library is: its postal address in address_as_written, its town in place_as_written, and the MaxPlace in place_id; only on a source whose source_type is archive or library, or other for a church office, government office, cemetery, family papers or a private collection, and never a person's home address.

parent_source_id.description: The larger MaxSource this one is part of, such as the collection that holds this series.

description.description: What this source holds and who it serves, in plain words.

embedding_text.description: Plain text built from the name, description and coverage, for search indexes.

bibliographic.description: How the work is cited: title, creators, publisher and edition.

holdings.description: The repositories that hold this source, with call numbers.

coverage.description: What the source covers, including, for each place, which years it holds and the exact words to search with (routing lives only here).

access.description: How the source is reached, and the polite way to search it.

link_status.description: Whether the source's address still works; a dead link is marked, never deleted.

last_verified_at.description: When the address was last confirmed to work.

discovered_via.description: How this source entry was first found.

discovered_via_as_written.description: How it was found, in the writer's own words, given when discovered_via is other.

external_ref.description: The link, category path or article title where this entry was found.

attribution.description: Credit to the human who compiled or contributed this entry (a credit never sets the living flag).

media_refs.description: Files that show this source (a title page, a repository photograph), each described once on the record that captured it.

title.description: The work's title, as it gives it.

creators.description: The people or bodies who made the work, in the order it names them.

publication_place_as_written.description: Where it was published, as written.

publication_date.description: When it was published (use derivation interpreted when the date is not quoted from the work).

abbreviation.description: A short title used in citations.

medium_as_written.description: The medium (book, microfilm, web page, manuscript), as written.

series.description: The series the work belongs to, as written.

volume_count.description: How many volumes the work has.

bibliographic.description: How a published or archival work is cited.

name_as_written.description: The creator's name exactly as the work gives it.

role.description: What this creator did for the work.

role_as_written.description: The creator's role in the work's own words, given when role is other.

creator.description: One creator of a work (a credit, which never sets a living flag).

repository_source_id.description: The repository's own MaxSource, when there is one.

holds_original.description: True when this repository is the custodian of the original (never a publisher, reseller or website); the original key's repo part comes from it.

call_number.description: The repository's call number or shelf mark.

medium_as_written.description: The medium held there (original volumes, microfilm, images), as written.

holding.description: One repository that holds this source.

places.description: The places covered, each with its years and the words to search with.

items.description: One kind of record held, in plain words or a MaxRecord record_type value.

record_types.description: The kinds of record the source holds.

span.description: The whole period the source covers (use derivation interpreted when the span is not quoted from the source).

languages.description: The languages of the records held, as language tags.

items.description: One group the source focuses on, in plain words.

ethnic_or_religious_groups.description: Any ethnic or religious focus of the records held.

record_count_estimate.description: The source's own count of the records it holds; left out when unknown, never guessed.

place.description: The place covered, as written (a MaxPlace id is attached later by the helper).

span.description: The years this source holds for this place.

search_as.description: The exact words to search with for this place, such as the made-up 'filed under Wrenshire county, not Tumblebrook'.

note.description: Anything else a researcher must know about this place in this source.

coverage_place.description: One place a source covers, with its routing.

access_method.description: The main way in; prefer api or bulk_download over scrape_only when they are offered.

access_method_as_written.description: The way in, in the writer's own words, given when access_method is other.

requires_auth.description: True when searching needs a login (agents never handle passwords).

api_base_url.description: The base address of the source's machine interface, when it has one.

robots_allowed.description: Whether the site's robots rules allow automated access to the pages concerned.

tos_url.description: The address of the source's terms of use.

crawl_notes.description: Politeness, rate-limit and method notes for automated searching.
